Optimal.Notes: The 40 fps / 40 Hz lock is the sweet spot for War Thunder on Deck, giving smooth gameplay in most battle types while keeping the APU from thermal throttling. Ground RB in large maps may dip slightly; reduce grass quality further if needed.

profiles.Summary: War Thunder runs well on the Steam Deck as a Verified title, benefiting from full controller support and relatively modest GPU requirements that the RDNA 2 APU can handle at medium settings. The game is an online-only MMO combat title, so a stable internet connection is required, and performance can vary between ground, air, and naval battles.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements versus Deck hardware capabilities and the Verified rating. On your first session, check frame pacing in a full ground battle lobby — if fps drops below 30 consistently, drop to Max Battery settings or reduce Shadow and Grass Quality further.

MaxBattery.Notes: Dropping to a 30 Hz refresh and 7 W TDP with a reduced render resolution upscaled via FSR maximises battery life. Air battles will generally run better than dense ground battles at these settings.

KnownIssues: Online-only requirement means no offline play; connection quality directly affects experience.
Game uses its own launcher/updater which can occasionally cause issues under Proton.
Large install size (~70–95 GB) and frequent updates may require significant storage management.
VR mode is non-functional on Steam Deck but does not affect standard play.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full native resolution at 60 Hz is achievable in air battles and lighter scenarios, but busy ground battles with many vehicles and explosions will drop into the 40s; the 60 fps cap prevents runaway GPU load. Battery life is short at 15 W TDP, so keep a charger handy for long sessions.

Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz gives perfectly smooth, tear-free gameplay that suits War Thunder's pace well. FSR upscaling from a modest render resolution keeps the GPU comfortably within the TDP budget even in larger battles.

profiles.Summary: War Thunder runs well on the Steam Deck as a Verified title, with its relatively modest minimum requirements sitting within the Deck's capabilities, though online multiplayer and busy battle scenes can push the GPU hard. Expect solid 40–60 fps at medium settings in most game modes, with heavier naval and combined-arms battles requiring lower settings to stay stable.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from War Thunder's PC minimum/recommended requirements and the Steam Deck's RDNA 2 GPU capabilities. On your first session, check frame rates during a busy ground battle — if you see sustained dips below your cap, drop to the Optimal or Max Battery profile and reduce Shadows Quality first.

MaxBattery.Notes: Running at a sub-native render resolution upscaled via the Deck's FSR filter with a low TDP cap maximises battery life. Grass and shadows are the biggest GPU costs in War Thunder and are cut first.

KnownIssues: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC requirements and hardware analysis.
Busy combined-arms battles with many vehicles and effects can cause frame dips on the Deck GPU.
The game's launcher/updater may occasionally require extra interaction before launching under Proton.
Online multiplayer requires a stable network connection; Wi-Fi inconsistency on Deck can cause lag in matches.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at high settings is achievable in most air and ground battles, but very large combined-arms or naval engagements may dip into the 40s; dropping Shadows Quality to Low is the fastest way to recover frames.
